minutes.headline: Board renewed the school-project bond note and pulled a final contractor payment over unresolved building defects.
minutes.summary: The Select Board heard a Council on Aging mission and goals presentation, ratified a senior tax work-off committee appointment, opened the May annual Town Meeting warrant, and renewed the bond anticipation note for the middle/high school project. A member questioned the final contractor payment over ceiling stains and punch-list items, and the signature on that warrant was crossed out. A resident questioned the borrowing, and officials explained final bonding awaits the MSBA audit.

what_happened.line: The Select Board renewed the bond anticipation note for the middle/high school project, as presented, by a passed vote.
The Board agreed to hold the final school-project payment warrant, and a member crossed out the signature, pending building committee answers on leaks.
The Board opened the warrant for the May 5, 2018 annual Town Meeting by a passed vote.
A resident asked why the note is being renewed; officials said final bonding awaits the MSBA audit and that authorized borrowing exceeded actual borrowing.
The Board ratified a senior property tax work-off committee appointment and heard a Council on Aging mission and goals presentation.

why_it_matters: The school building project is still not finally financed, so the town carries short-term note borrowing and its interest cost until the MSBA audit sets the final reimbursement and bonding.
Holding the last contractor payment over reported leaks and punch-list items bears on whether the town pays in full for work that residents will own and maintain.
The May Town Meeting warrant is now open, and the budget calendar for the coming year will lead to votes residents are asked to take.
watch_next: The building committee's answers on school leaks at the next Select Board meeting, and the held final payment warrant.
The Finance Committee meetings targeted for January 25 and March 29 for a possible quorum.
